name: post_halt_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: When a stock hits its upper or lower circuit limit and trading is halted on NSE/BSE, there is an information asymmetry: the halt indicates extreme demand/supply imbalance, but the price has been artificially frozen. When the halt is lifted (or on the next trading session if the halt persists to close), the first 5-10 minutes show strong momentum continuation in ~65% of cases as the pent-up order flow resolves. The inefficiency exists because retail traders fear post-halt volatility and avoid trading, while institutional participants with faster systems capture the continuation. For partial halts (stock reopens after 45-min cooling period), the reopening bar provides a tradeable momentum signal.
universe: All NSE F&O stocks that hit circuit limits intraday
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹25 Cr; stock must have been halted due to price movement (not regulatory/technical halt); F&O listed

indicators.name: Halt_Direction
indicators.params: +1 if upper circuit hit; -1 if lower circuit hit

indicators.name: Pre_Halt_Momentum
indicators.params: ROC(close, 15) at the time of halt (how fast was the move)

conditions: Halt_Direction == +1 (upper circuit was hit — bullish halt)
Reopen_Gap >= 0 (stock reopens at or above halt price — demand persists)
Reopen_Volume_Ratio > 2.0 (high volume at reopening — genuine interest)
long.confirmation: First 2 bars after reopen close above reopen_price (momentum sustained)

conditions: Halt_Direction == -1 (lower circuit was hit — bearish halt)
Reopen_Gap <= 0 (stock reopens at or below halt price — supply persists)
short.confirmation: First 2 bars after reopen close below reopen_price

exit.target: 50 bps from entry (post-halt moves tend to be large)
exit.stop_loss: 30 bps from entry (quick exit if halt momentum fades)
exit.trailing_stop: After 30 bps profit, trail at 15 bps from high-water mark
exit.time_stop: 30 bars (30 min — post-halt momentum dissipates quickly)

risk.position_sizing: Reduced size ₹75K due to higher volatility; decrease to ₹50K if VIX > 20

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; during market-wide panic (VIX > 25), circuit breaks may be systemic and continuation less reliable
filters.time_filter: Halt reopen must be at least 30 min before market close (reopen after 14:45 IST: skip)
filters.volume_filter: Reopen_Volume_Ratio > 2.0 (sufficient volume to confirm genuine interest, not just market makers)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 direction should agree with halt direction (bull market + upper circuit = stronger; bear market + upper circuit = weaker signal)
filters.spread_filter: Post-reopen bid-ask spread < 15 bps (wider than normal due to uncertainty)
filters.event_filter: Skip if halt is due to corporate action (bonus, split) rather than market forces
other_filters: Stock must not have hit circuit on previous day (avoid serial circuit hitters where price discovery is impaired)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — trading halts are episodic and unpredictable; each event is unique; difficult to build systematic algo around rare events, which reduces competition

weaknesses: Trading halts are rare events (0-3 per day across entire F&O universe) — the strategy may go days without a signal, making it unviable as a standalone strategy
Post-halt spreads are significantly wider (10-20 bps vs normal 3-5 bps), increasing slippage costs and potentially eating the edge

Lower circuit halts in particular can be caused by genuinely bad news (fraud, regulatory action) where the momentum continuation is a trap — the stock may be down for fundamental reasons with further downside
prior_art: Corwin & Lipson (2000) on trading halts; Lee, Ready & Seguin (1994) on volume and volatility around halts; Indian circuit breaker mechanism studied by NSE working papers; post-halt drift documented in various markets
notes: This strategy should be combined with other strategies as part of a portfolio approach given its low frequency. Consider using options instead of equity for post-halt trades to define risk more precisely. The order book data at reopen is critical for assessing demand/supply balance.
